title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Sharma
description: Context: This PR bundles three coordinated changes to reduce per-token unit economics for common workloads: 1) introduce autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching policies, 2) add model-aware quantization profile presets and a migration path, and 3) expose a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) toolkit to help operators evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs and validate regressions. Motivation: customers frequently see suboptimal defaults for new workloads (small requests, high concurrency) and selecting quantization/atomic batch sizes is error-prone. The goal is to provide safe defaults that lower cost by ~10-40% across a range of production workloads and give platform operators visibility to tune further. What changed (high-level): - runtime/autotune: new policy engine that observes request size distribution, p50/p95 latency, and model KV hit rates and recommends a config (batch_size, max_wait_ms, cache_ttl, cache_capacity). - serving/quant: adds quantization profiles (fp16, int8-q4_0, int8-q4_1 presets) per model-family and runtime compatibility metadata; includes a migration helper to switch traffic to quant variants with fallback. - tools/uecon: CLI + API to simulate unit-econ with historical traces, produce per-route cost/latency delta reports, and output suggested rollout percentages for canaries. - console: new per-model suggestions panel and a UECon report link in route details. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-2189) approved - [x] perf benchmarks run on perf-canary (S3/GPU cluster) - [x] safety: fallback to pinned model variant if QoS degrades >5% p95 - [x] telemetry hooks and audit logs added - [x] docs and quickstart updated Implementation notes: - The autotune engine runs in the control plane as a non-blocking background task; it emits suggestions and an optional automatic mode that writes configs subject to guardrails. - Quant profiles are additive: models keep exact-precision variants; profiles are applied per-deployment and signed to ensure compatibility. - The uecon toolkit uses sampled request traces (rate-limited) to run micro-simulations locally and produces an expected cost delta with 90% CI. Rollout plan: feature is behind an org-level feature flag (autotune:enabled). Default for new orgs is enabled; existing orgs are opt-in via console or API. We will gradually enable automatic writes for orgs that opt in after 2 weeks of suggestions monitoring. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: autotune picks an aggressive batching policy that increases p95 under bursty traffic. Mitigation: conservative ramping and a rollback window if p95 regresses >5% within 1 hour. - Risk: quantized model introduces small quality regressions. Mitigation: quality check harness in eval-harness and canary routing with golden prompts. Related: ENG-2189, ENG-2190, SUP-5472. Summary of impact: targeted customers (high-throughput embedding pipelines, chat endpoints with high concurrency) should see 10-40% cost reduction with no observable QoS impact in canaries. See release_notes for items to communicate to customers.

release_notes:
- Autotune defaults: safer batching + KV-prefix caching defaults that reduce unit cost for many workloads.
- Quantization profiles: model-aware presets and migration helper to safely roll to quant variants.
- UECon toolkit: CLI and API to simulate and report expected cost/latency deltas with rollout suggestions.
- Opt-in rollout and conservative guardrails: default off for existing orgs; automatic writes roll out after monitoring.
